title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary: This PR implements an end-to-end set of changes to automate cost-optimization defaults across the serving stack: autotuned batching and prefix/KV caching defaults, a new set of quantization profiles and selection logic, and a lightweight unit-economics (UEcon) tooling endpoint + CLI helper so engineering teams can evaluate tradeoffs.

Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/caching/quant manually which is error prone and hard to reproduce across deployments (hosted, dedicated, private). We want safe defaults and an automation path that picks a profile given workload signals and cost targets. This PR wires together runtime heuristics, model metadata, and an admin-facing UEcon API to recommend and apply profiles.

What changed (high level):
- Runtime: added AutotuneManager that computes batching window, max_batch_size, and prefix_cache TTL based on recent request distribution and configured latency SLOs. Implemented gradual rollout with canary percent and cooldown.
- Quantization: added three curated quant profiles (q5_0_fast, q4_0_cost, q3_0_ultra) with metadata describing memory/speed/quality tradeoffs. Added profile selection logic that factors unit cost and estimated quality delta.
- UEcon tooling: added /admin/uecon/recommend endpoint and a small CLI command redwood uecon simulate which runs synthetic load against a model and returns estimated cost/latency/quality deltas for candidate profiles.
- Config: new defaults in config/runtime_autotune.yaml and model registry annotations for quant profiles and preferred default SLOs.
- Tests and docs: integration tests for AutotuneManager and CLI, updated docs + examples in docs/cost-optimization.md.

Commits (summary):
- 3b7d2f1: feat(runtime): AutotuneManager core loop and policy evaluation
- 5c9a1b4: feat(quant): add quant profiles + selection scoring
- a47f8d0: feat(uecon): add admin endpoint and CLI simulate command
- d1e4f6b: fix(tests): stabilize timing mocks for CI
- f12b3e6: docs: cost optimization page + examples

Files changed (high level):
- packages/runtime/src/autotune_manager.py - new
- packages/runtime/tests/test_autotune.py - new
- services/model-registry/data/quant_profiles.yaml - new
- services/admin-service/handlers/uecon.py - new
- tools/redwood-cli/commands/uecon.py - new
- config/runtime_autotune.yaml - modified
- docs/cost-optimization.md - modified
- packages/runtime/metrics/metric_keys.py - modified (added autotune metrics)

Review conversation (high-level excerpts):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Overall looks good. Two asks: add a fallback if profile selection returns a negative quality delta without confidence, and add observability for cooldown windows. Also please add a short note about safety for private deployments."
- Maya (author): "Addressed both: added conservative fallback to keep current profile when confidence < 0.6 and emitted autotune.cooldown metric. Added note in docs and tests to ensure private deployments require explicit opt-in via config flag."
- Sofia Ramirez (reviewer): "Can you ensure the CLI returns machine-readable JSON when --json is passed? We need this for automation in infra pipelines."
- Maya: "Added --json flag and tests."
- Arjun Desai (reviewer): "Observed flaky test in CI due to timing; please make test less timing-dependent."
- Maya: "Reworked tests to use deterministic mocking for clock and request traces."
- Final approvals: Liam, Sofia, Arjun approved. Merge approved by oncall.

CI summary: initial CI run (linux unit) failed due to timing-dependent test (test_autotune::test_cooldown). I pushed d1e4f6b to stabilize mocks; rerun succeeded. Full CI: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-e2e: pass, lint: pass, security-scan: pass. Artifact: new quant_profiles.yaml included in model-registry artifact bundle. Merge: squash and merge performed by Maya. Merge commit: f9e4b3c.

Release notes: - Added autotune defaults for batching and caching to reduce manual tuning burden and decrease cost under typical traffic patterns. - Introduced curated quantization profiles and runtime selection logic to balance cost and quality. - Added UEcon admin endpoint and CLI tooling to estimate per-model unit economics for candidate profiles and defaults.

Backwards compatibility and safety: All changes are opt-in for private deployments (requires runtime.autotune.enabled=true). Hosted customers get conservative defaults rolled out through feature flag with gradual canary. There are no breaking API changes. The config file adds new keys with sensible defaults.

release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching/caching, curated quant profiles with selection logic, and UEcon admin + CLI tooling to evaluate cost/quality tradeoffs.
notes_for_release: Hosted rollout: feature-flag gated; gradual canary across 10% -> 50% -> 100% based on metrics
Dedicated clusters: default enabled but can be disabled via runtime.autotune.enabled=false
Private deployments: requires explicit opt-in; documented in docs/cost-optimization.md
